page: Microsoft Azure D48_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 48 vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz, utilizing hyper-threading with two threads per core. The compute hardware is coupled with 192.0 GB of memory, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The CPU configuration provides a 35 MB L3 cache and supports modern vector extensions including AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI. The instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators and includes no bundled local temporary storage, requiring external Azure managed disks for persistence.

Benchmark results demonstrate steady multi-threaded capacity and strong uncached memory write throughput. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 38,358.2 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,715.0, placing it solidly in the middle tier of general compute performance. Memory subsystems show strong capability on large uncached blocks, reaching 92.68 GB/sec on sequential write operations. In contrast, single-thread compute metrics are restrained, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring 1,405.08, falling in the bottom 25% percentile. Furthermore, CPU-based LLM text generation performs poorly, sustaining only 5.15 tokens per second on a 7B parameter model.

Given its high core count and sizable memory footprint balanced against moderate per-core clock performance, the D48_v4 offers solid resource density for multi-threaded applications. The absence of local disk requires planning for remote storage latency and costs, making the instance an effective platform for parallelized enterprise workloads, in-memory caching platforms such as Redis (which benchmarks at 40.96 million SET ops/sec), compilation pipelines, and containerized web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure D48_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 48 vCPUs (24 physical cores) powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz, supported by 192.0 GB of RAM. The instance features a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, a 35 MB L3 cache, and AVX-512 support. It includes no bundled local storage and no GPU accelerators, relying on remote storage for disk I/O. Benchmark assessments show solid multi-core execution (Geekbench multi-core score of 11,715.0) and strong uncached memory write bandwidth of 92.68 GB/sec, offset by lower single-core benchmark scores and weak LLM generation throughput. The instance is structured for multi-threaded workloads, in-memory caches, software compilation, and scalable web serving.
